question: Why do most web maps stop at about 85 degrees north and south, leaving the poles off?
answer: To make the world a square. On Mercator's map the poles lie infinitely far away, so web maps cut it where its height equals its width: at 85.05°. That turns the world into square tiles that zoom neatly, at the cost of the polar regions and huge distortion near them.
move: Every map trades something away; ask what this one gave up.
ask: Which smooth tool have I used without noticing what it quietly leaves out?
source: Battersby et al., Implications of Web Mercator and its use in online mapping, Cartographica, 2014
